messages:
Maya (support): Customer report: ACME-EU was charged 21% VAT on invoice 2025-0421 even though they supplied a validated BE VAT number (BE0123456789) on 2025-04-21. Ticket #INC-5821 created. Need quick triage, customer expects reverse-charge (0%).

Liam (billing): Can you paste the invoice JSON / tax lines and the VAT ID validation result? Did the frontend show 'VAT validated'?

Maya (support): Frontend showed green check and saved VAT ID. Pasted invoice snippet below from billing service logs: 
```
{"invoice_id":"2025-0421","customer_id":"ACME-EU","amount_total_cents":100000,"tax_amount_cents":21000,"tax_rate":0.21,"tax_exemption":false}
```
VAT validation microservice returns: `{"vat_id":"BE0123456789","valid":true,"country":"BE"}`. Customer also attached the PO which marks B2B reverse charge.

billing-bot: New payment processed via Stripe PM card_1JkX.. country: "GB"; charge_id: ch_1JkX..

Sofia (eng): Looking at the tax calc logs for invoice 2025-0421. The tax engine selected `tax_country=payment_method.card.country` (GB) instead of `customer.vat_country` (BE) because there was a PM update event between save steps. Repro steps I used: 1) Save VAT ID on account 2) Add card with GB BIN 3) Trigger invoice -> tax engine picks card country when `customer.billing_country` is null and we currently prefer `payment_method.country` in that code path.

Sofia (eng): Repro snippet: 
```
# simplified pseudo-log
fetch_customer(ACME-EU) -> vat_country=BE
fetch_payment_method(card_1JkX) -> country=GB
if not billing_country: tax_country = payment_method.country  # current behavior
compute_tax(tax_country) -> apply 21% (GB fallback mapped to VAT 21%)
```

Liam (billing): So this is a precedence bug. If customer has validated VAT ID we must use VAT country and mark tax_exempt=true (reverse-charge). Is there a quick defensive patch we can roll?

Sofia (eng): Yes. Quick patch: change precedence in tax resolver to `customer.vat_country` (if validated) -> `customer.billing_country` -> `payment_method.country`. Add unit test for race (pm update during checkout). I can ship as hotfix to staging today, prod after sign-off.

Eric (finance): Customer requested immediate remediation and refund. We should issue a credit note for 21% on invoice 2025-0421 and refund the tax portion of the charge (210.00 EUR). Confirm process: create credit note, post to accounting, then refund via payment provider. Also need note to customer explaining error and expected timeline.

Liam (billing): I'll generate the credit note draft and queue refund. Which refund flow do we use for card charges? Full refund vs partial? We only refund tax portion. Refund docs: `POST /v1/refunds` with `amount=21000` and `reason=tax_misapplied`.

Maya (support): Customer message: they prefer credit note and invoice correction, not forcing chargeback. Will communicate timeline: 3 business days for refund via Stripe, credit note issued immediately.

Sofia (eng): FYI, this path is rare but reproducible when a PM add/update webhook arrives between vat save and invoice generation. I'll also add an event correlation guard (use the customer object snapshot at invoice creation). Plan: patch -> test -> deploy to prod tonight (low traffic window).

billing-bot: Created credit-note CN-2025-0421-1 for invoice 2025-0421 (amount_cents:21000). Refund queued: refund_1JkX.. pending.

Eric (finance): I'll post the journal entries after refund clears. Also creating a monitoring alert for tax-calc mismatches (invoice tax != expected tax given validated VAT status).

Maya (support): I'll update the customer: "We found a precedence bug in our tax calculation that caused your card country to be used. We've issued a credit note CN-2025-0421-1 and initiated a refund for €210. You should see funds in 3-5 business days. We will deploy a fix tonight and add monitoring to prevent recurrence."

Liam (billing): Follow-ups: 1) QA confirm credit note correctness 2) Finance sign-off on posting 3) Eng deploy patch 4) Add unit & integration test to prevent regressions. Assigning owners: Liam (credit), Eric (accounting), Sofia (fix), Maya (customer comms).

Sofia (eng): I'll open PR and link to this thread. PR will include change log and test vectors (cases: validated BE VAT, validated non-EU VAT, missing VAT -> fallback to billing address, pm-country fallback).

Maya (support): Customer acknowledged and thanked us. Marking issue as active, will close when refund clears and fix is deployed. :white_check_mark:
